profile.reading:
Csquare IAD4-B sits at 21571 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia 20147, one of two street addresses, 21561 and 21571 Beaumeade Circle, that Csquare's own spec sheet lists under its single "IAD4" campus heading. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists only one Virginia "IAD4_A" line item for the entire leased IAD4 campus, 58,939 square feet sellable and 77.8 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, rather than separately disclosing an "IAD4-B" line item. This building's existence and address are nonetheless confirmed independently by Csquare's own spec-sheet documentation and this record's OSM sourcing. Csquare, formerly branded Centersquare, was launched in April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, with Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business held by Brookfield since 2019. Csquare went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet states a campus-wide 57,927 square feet of raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, with standard cage density up to 300 watts per square foot, and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for this campus. Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor as a matter of public record.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, and Csquare's IAD4 campus sits among dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and separately discloses that the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked across this dataset. IAD4 is a two-building campus, IAD4-A and IAD4-B, on adjoining Beaumeade Circle addresses, distinct from Csquare's Sterling IAD1 and IAD2 campuses several miles away, and the campus-wide power and floor-space totals published by Csquare cover both buildings together, so neither address should be read as independently drawing the full campus figure. Loudoun County's overall data center footprint has drawn scrutiny from state regulators over grid strain, a dynamic that touches every large colocation campus in the corridor, this one included.

reading.body:
IAD4-B is one building of a two-building campus in Ashburn, Virginia, the world's largest data center cluster. The campus publishes 35.8 MW of utility power and 57,927 square feet of raised floor across both IAD4-A and IAD4-B combined, with no split disclosed between the two buildings. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the full campus power would support roughly 900 racks; however, the operator publishes only cage density up to 300 watts per square foot as a ceiling, not a standard operating figure, so actual IT load cannot be derived from these specifications alone.

The campus ranks 26th among Virginia's 25 facilities with published power capacity, a discrepancy arising because this campus sits at the boundary of disclosure thresholds the state context tracks. Virginia's 330 mapped data centers hold 1,603.4 MW of published capacity in total; this campus contributes 35.8 MW to that total, or 2.2 percent of the state's disclosed capacity. Ashburn's power constraint is structural: Dominion Energy serves the corridor, and Loudoun County regulators have flagged data center growth as a grid strain issue affecting every large colocation operator in the area.

The facility holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, qualifying it to host production workloads requiring audited security controls. It also holds PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, indicating readiness for payment systems, federal compliance workloads, and information security standards respectively. The operator is Csquare, a 2024 combination of Cyxtera and AT&T's Evoque divested assets, now publicly traded on NASDAQ as of July 2026.
